rom_sha1_executed_note: The clean case booted the overlay 29ea04c2. The swap case booted the randomized cartridge 0d75313f; the two flipped cases were temp copies of it with sha1 87f75ccd... and 26d62ad1.... All four derive from the 29ea04c2 overlay.

synth: All four cases use stage 1 only. The fixture is run 1's overlay fixture (clean) or s29 (the rest), so the same SYNTH save as R2.
The two flipped ROMs were temp copies made under r3/ and deleted after the runs; the Manager's roms/a.gbc was never touched.

why_two_layers: The two refusals are at different layers and that is the point: the server can only compare a cartridge against the contract it was launched with (swap), while the client compares the cartridge against the beacon the overlay itself published (both flips). A cartridge with a valid contract but a modified overlay is stopped by the client, not the server.
not_proven: A cartridge that is both contract-valid and beacon-valid but semantically wrong (e.g. randomized without the Manager) is out of scope here.
The refusals were observed against the 29ea04c2 overlay; the beacon bytes changed with the phone-card commit.
